proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof; Simon Ch. 4, 2.5–2.7 (chapter-04.txt lines 157–210: if V is stationary in U ∩ N then ∫div_M X dμ_V = −∫X·H̄_N dμ_V with H̄_N = Σ_i B_x(τ_i, τ_i)) and Ch. 4, 3.3–3.6, 3.14–3.17 (chapter-04.txt lines 255–320 and 370–430: monotonicity with bounded mean curvature). Uses the sibling imrep_mass_and_support. Notation: T_xM is the approximate tangent space, which where it exists equals approxTangentPlane n M x (uniqueness); for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM, div_M X(x) = Σ_i⟨τ_i, DX(x)τ_i⟩ = tangentialDivergence; P(q) denotes the orthogonal projection onto T_qN.
1. Local geometry of N and the constants. Let (V₀, W₀, ψ) be a chart of N at y₀ from IsEmbeddedSubmanifold 2 (n+ℓ) N: ψ is C², injective, proper onto W₀ ∩ N = ψ(V₀), with injective differential. Hence N ∩ W₀ is an embedded C² submanifold, T_qN = Dψ(v)(ℝ^{n+ℓ}) for q = ψ(v) (C¹ curves in N ∩ W₀ lift through a local C¹ inverse of ψ), and q ↦ P(q) is C¹ along N ∩ W₀ (P(ψ(v)) = Dψ(v)(Dψ(v)ᵀDψ(v))⁻¹Dψ(v)ᵀ). Choose r_a > 0 with B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) ⊆ U ∩ W₀. Because (N̄ ∖ N) ∩ U = ∅, N ∩ B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) = N̄ ∩ B̄_{8r_a}(y₀) is compact. By the tubular neighbourhood theorem for C² submanifolds (R. L. Foote, Proc. AMS 92 (1984) 153–155; G. Leobacher and A. Steinicke, Ann. Global Anal. Geom. 60 (2021) 559–587, arXiv:1811.10578: the nearest point projection onto a C^k submanifold is C^{k−1} near it), after decreasing r_a every x ∈ B_{4r_a}(y₀) has a unique nearest point π(x) ∈ N (it lies in N ∩ B_{8r_a}(y₀) because dist(x, N) ≤ |x − y₀|), π : B_{4r_a}(y₀) → N is C¹, π(q) = q and Dπ(q) = P(q) for q ∈ N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀). Then Π := P∘π is C¹ on B_{4r_a}(y₀) and Π = P on N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀). For q ∈ N ∩ B_{4r_a}(y₀) and u, v ∈ T_qN put B_q(u, v) := (D_uP)(q)v (derivative of P along N). Differentiating P² = P shows P(q)(D_uP)(q)u = 0, so B_q(u, u) ⊥ T_qN; and |B_q(u, v)| ≤ β|u||v| with β := sup ‖DP‖ over N ∩ B̄_{4r_a}(y₀) < ∞ (continuity on a compact set). Set r₀ := r_a and κ := nβ; then B̄_{3r₀}(y₀) ⊆ U.
2. M ⊆ N up to a null set. Fix T, R as in the statement. By imrep_mass_and_support (ii), spt T = U ∩ spt μ_R. As μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt μ_R) = 0 (second countability; Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support) and μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ U) = 0 (M ⊆ U), μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt T) = 0; with spt T ⊆ N this gives μ_R(ℝ^{n+k} ∖ N) = 0, i.e. Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (θ ≥ 1 on M).
3. Approximate tangent spaces lie in T_xN. Let G₀ be the set of x ∈ M ∩ N at which T_xM exists and is oriented by ξ(x) (R.orients); Hⁿ(M ∖ G₀) = 0 by step 2. Let x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀) and v ∈ T_xM with |v| = 1. Since Hⁿ⌞(M ∖ N) = 0, the blow-ups of Hⁿ⌞M at x are those of Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ N). For each s ∈ (0, 1/2), the sets η_{x,λ}(M ∩ N) meet B_s(v) for all small λ > 0: otherwise, along some λ_i ↓ 0, ∫_{η_{x,λ_i}(M)} f dHⁿ = 0 for an f ∈ C_c(B_s(v)) with f ≥ 0, f(v) > 0, contradicting convergence to ∫_{T_xM} f dHⁿ > 0. So v = lim (x_i − x)/λ_i with x_i ∈ M ∩ N, x_i → x, |x_i − x|/λ_i → 1. Since N ∩ W₀ is a C¹ submanifold, the unit vectors (x_i − x)/|x_i − x| accumulate only in T_xN; hence v ∈ T_xN, and T_xM ⊆ T_xN.
4. Definition of H. For x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀) let H(x) := Σ_{i=1}^n B_x(τ_i, τ_i) for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM ⊆ T_xN. This does not depend on the basis, since it equals Σ_{a,b}(P_{T_xM})_{ab}·B_x(P(x)e_a, P(x)e_b). Put H(x) := 0 at all other points. Then |H(x)| ≤ nβ = κ for every x. H is μ_R-a.e. strongly measurable: P_{T_xM} = Σ_i τ_iτ_iᵀ is a continuous function of the unit simple n-vector ξ(x) = ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ (the sign cancels), ξ is a.e. strongly measurable, and x ↦ B_x is continuous on N ∩ B̄_{4r₀}(y₀).
5. First variation formula (a) (Simon 2.7). Let X be C¹ with compact support, spt X ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). Define X^T(x) := Π(x)X(x) for x ∈ B_{4r₀}(y₀) and X^T(x) := 0 otherwise. X^T is C¹: it is C¹ on the open set B_{4r₀}(y₀), it vanishes on the open set ℝ^{n+k} ∖ spt X, and these two open sets cover ℝ^{n+k}. Its support lies in spt X, a compact subset of U, and X^T(x) ∈ T_xN for every x ∈ N ∩ U (X^T(x) = P(x)X(x) if x ∈ N ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀), and X^T(x) = 0 otherwise). Stationarity (R.IsStationaryAlong N) gives δV(X^T) = 0. Let Y := X − X^T, which equals (I − Π)X on B_{4r₀}(y₀). Let x ∈ G₀ ∩ B_{4r₀}(y₀), and let τ be an orthonormal basis of T_xM ⊆ T_xN. Then DY(x)τ_i = −(DΠ(x)τ_i)X(x) + (I − P(x))DX(x)τ_i. We have ⟨τ_i, (I − P(x))w⟩ = 0 for all w. Also DΠ(x)τ_i = DP(x)[Dπ(x)τ_i] = (D_{τ_i}P)(x), because Dπ(x) = P(x) is the identity on T_xN. Since (D_{τ_i}P)(x) is symmetric, ⟨τ_i, (D_{τ_i}P)(x)X(x)⟩ = ⟨B_x(τ_i, τ_i), X(x)⟩. Hence div_M Y(x) = −⟨X(x), H(x)⟩. The same identity holds at μ_R-a.e. x outside B_{4r₀}(y₀): there X and Y vanish near x, so both sides are 0. The integrands θ·div_M X^T and θ·div_M Y are bounded and vanish off the compact set spt X, so δV is additive on them and δV(X) = δV(X^T) + δV(Y) = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ_R. This proves (a).
6. Monotonicity (b) (Simon 3.3–3.6, 3.16–3.17). Fix z ∈ B_{r₀}(y₀) and R_z with r₀ < R_z < 2r₀ − |z − y₀|, so B̄_{R_z}(z) ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). Let g : ℝ → [0, 1] be C¹ and nondecreasing with g = 0 on (−∞, 0] and g = 1 on [1, ∞). For ε ∈ (0, 1) let γ_ε(t) := g((1 − t)/ε): γ_ε is C¹ and nonincreasing, γ_ε = 1 on (−∞, 1 − ε], γ_ε = 0 on [1, ∞), and γ_ε increases to the indicator of (−∞, 1) as ε ↓ 0. With r(x) := |x − z| and s ∈ (0, R_z), the field X_s(x) := γ_ε(r/s)(x − z) is C¹ (γ_ε(r/s) is constant near z) and spt X_s ⊆ B̄_s(z) ⊆ B_{2r₀}(y₀). At μ_R-a.e. x, div_M X_s = nγ_ε(r/s) + (r/s)γ_ε'(r/s)(1 − |∇^⊥r|²), where ∇^⊥r is the component of ∇r orthogonal to T_xM. Let I(s) := ∫γ_ε(r/s) dμ_R and J(s) := ∫γ_ε(r/s)|∇^⊥r|² dμ_R. These are finite and, by dominated convergence, differentiable in s, with sI'(s) = −∫(r/s)γ_ε'(r/s) dμ_R and sJ'(s) = −∫(r/s)γ_ε'(r/s)|∇^⊥r|² dμ_R ≥ 0. By (a), nI(s) − sI'(s) + sJ'(s) = δV(X_s) = −∫γ_ε(r/s)⟨x − z, H⟩ dμ_R. Hence (s^{−n}I)'(s) = s^{−n−1}(sJ'(s) + ∫γ_ε(r/s)⟨x − z, H⟩ dμ_R) ≥ −κ s^{−n}I(s), because J' ≥ 0 and |⟨x − z, H⟩| ≤ κs on the support of γ_ε(r/s). Therefore (e^{κs}s^{−n}I(s))' ≥ 0 on (0, R_z), and e^{κσ}σ^{−n}I(σ) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) for 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r₀. Letting ε ↓ 0, I(s) increases to μ_R(B_s(z)) (monotone convergence). This gives (b) in [0, ∞]; both sides are finite because B̄_ρ(z) is a compact subset of U. (Equivalently, apply SimonGMT Chapter04/MeanCurvature.lean, HasGeneralizedMeanCurvatureIn.exp_normalizedBallMass_monotoneOn, for closed balls and take left limits.)
key_steps: Choose a C² chart and a C¹ nearest point retraction π near y₀; fix the second fundamental form bound β and set κ = nβ.
By the support identity, μ_R is carried by spt T ⊆ N, and a.e. approximate tangent space lies inside T_xN.
Split X = Π X + (I − Π)X: stationarity kills the tangential part, and the normal part gives div_M = −⟨X, H⟩ with H = Σ B(τ_i, τ_i), |H| ≤ κ.
The radial first variation with |H| ≤ κ makes e^{κs}s^{−n}μ_R(B_s(z)) nondecreasing.
